Definition: from G5219; attentively listening, i.e. (by implication) submissive:--obedient.
BiblicalUsage: The word hypḗkoos carries the sense of obedient, submissive, listening. In 2 Corinthians 2:9, the text says "whether ye be obedient in all things." In Philippians 2:8, the text says "and became obedient unto death."
TheologicalSignificance: What hypḗkoos teaches me is that obedience is not drudgery; it is trusting that God's way is the good way. That shapes how I read the passages where it appears: not as filler, but as God's own wording for what He is doing.
